==English== {{wp}} ===Etymology 1=== From {{inh|en|enm|or}}; partially contracted from {{m|enm|other}}, {{m|enm|auther}}, from {{inh|en|ang|āþor}}, {{m|ang|āwþer}}, {{m|ang|āhwæþer}} {{gloss|"some, any, either"; > {{l|en|either}}}}; and partially from {{inh|en|enm|oththe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|oþþe}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*efþau|t=or}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|fy|of|t=or}}, {{cog|cim|odar}}, {{m|cim|òdar|t=or}}, {{cog|nl|of}}, {{m|nl|oft}}, {{m|nl|ofte|t=or}}, {{cog|de,lb,wym|oder|t=or}}, {{cog|nds|of}}, {{m|nds|àder}}, {{l|nds|àr}}, {{l|nds|åder}}, {{m|nds|år|t=or}}, {{cog|yi|אָדער|t=or}}, {{cog|is|eða}}, {{m|is|eður|t=or}}, {{cog|got|𐌰𐌹𐌸𐌸𐌰𐌿|t=or; otherwise}}. {{col-bottom}} ====Pronunciation==== * {{a|en|RP}} ** {{IPA|en|/ə(ɹ)/|a=weak form}} ** {{IPA|en|/ɔː(ɹ)/|a=strong form}} ** {{audio|en|En-uk-or.ogg|a=strong form}} * {{a|en|GA}} ** {{IPA|en|/ɚ/|a=weak form}} ** {{IPA|en|/oɹ/|a=strong form}} ** {{audio|en|En-us-or.ogg|a=strong form}} *** {{IPA|en|/ɑɹ/|a=STL}} * {{a|en|CA}} ** {{IPA|en|[ɚ]|[əɹ]|a=weak form}} ** {{IPA|en|[oːɹ]|a=strong form}} *** {{IPA|en|[ɔ(ː)ɹ]|a=Dialectal}} * {{a|en|Pacific Northwest}} ** {{IPA|en|/ʔɹ/|/ʌɹ/|a=strong form}} * {{homophones|en|oar|ore|o'er|;|aw|awe}} * {{rhymes|en|ɔː(ɹ)|s=1}} ====Conjunction==== {{en-head|conj}} # {{n-g|Connects at least two alternative [[word]]s, [[phrase]]s, [[clause]]s, [[sentences]], [[etc.]], each of which could make a passage [[true]].}} #: {{ux|en|He might get cancer, '''or''' be hit by a bus, '''or''' God knows what.}} # {{lb|en|logic}} {{n-g|An operator denoting the [[disjunction]] of two [[propositions]] or [[truth values]]. There are two forms: the [[inclusive or]] and the [[exclusive or]].}} # {{n-g|Used to present two or more options from which a choice is to be made.}} #: {{ux|en|Do you want tea '''or''' coffee?}} #: {{ux|en|You may stay '''or''' go.}} # [[otherwise|Otherwise]] {{gloss|a consequence of the condition that the previous is false}}. #: {{ux|en|It's raining! Come inside '''or''' you'll catch a cold!}} #* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=IV|page=46|passage=No matter how early I came down, I would find him on the veranda, smoking cigarettes, '''or''' otherwise his man would be there with a message to say that his master would shortly join me if I would kindly wait.}} # {{n-g|Connects two equivalent names.}} #: {{ux|en|The country [[Myanmar]], '''or''' [[Burma]]}} ## {{lb|en|archaic}} ''Used in the title of a work after a short name to introduce an alternative name, generally one which is more descriptive. Typically preceded by a semicolon or colon and followed by a comma.'' ##* {{quote-book|en|author=w:Isaac Newton|title={{w|Opticks|Opticks: '''or''', A Treatise of the Reflexions, Refractions, Inflexions and Colours of Light}}|year=1704|nocolon=1|page_plain=title page|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/opticksortreatisnewt/page/n8/mode/1up}} ##* {{quote-book|en|author=w:Eliza Haywood|title={{w|Love in Excess; or, The Fatal Enquiry|Love in Excess; '''or''' The Fatal Enquiry}}|year=1719|nocolon=1|page_plain=title page|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/loveinexcessorfa00hayw/page/n4/mode/1up}} ##* {{quote-book|en|author=w:Samuel Richardson|title={{w|Pamela; or, Virtue Rewarded|Pamela; '''or''', Virtue Rewarded}}|year=1740|nocolon=1|page_plain=title page|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/richardsonpamela3ed04/page/n5/mode/1up}} ##* {{quote-book|en|author=w:Erasmus Darwin|title={{w|Zoonomia|Zoonomia; '''or''', the Laws of Organic Life}}|year=1794|nocolon=1|page_plain=title page|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/zoonomiaorlawsof1794darw/page/n4/mode/1up}} # {{n-g|Used in between two [[numbers]] to denote a [[range]] between them.}} #: {{ux|en|A man of 18 '''or''' 20 years}} =====Usage notes===== * {{s|connecting alternative terms}} When not implied by the meaning of the [[conjoin#Noun|conjoin]]s, it is generally ambiguous whether “or” is intended in an exclusive or inclusive sense. In speech, various means may be used to convey exclusivity, such as stress on the word “or” or a rising intonation before it.{{cite-book|en|last=Huddleston|first=Rodney|year=1988|title=English Grammar: An Outline|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=0521311527|pages=198–99}} In a formal or technical register, {{m|en|and/or}} may be used to specify inclusivity. =====Derived terms=====
